summary: Prepare for MLOps and AI platform roles: reproducible training and evaluation, deploying and serving models and LLM services, and monitoring quality, drift and cost.

topics.title: From experiment to production
points: Reproducible training: data, code and environment versions

topics.title: Serving models
topics.why: Expect questions on latency, scale and cost.
points: Serving LLMs: batching, caching and limits

topics.title: Monitoring models
topics.why: How you'd notice a model getting worse.

topics.title: Cloud certifications
topics.why: Optional, but a structured way to learn.
points: AWS Certified Machine Learning, Google Cloud ML Engineer, Azure AI Engineer: pick the cloud you use

exercises.title: Ship a model with a gate
exercises.goal: Have a pipeline story with evaluation.
steps: Train a small model on a public dataset in your code editor.
Track the run and save the model with its metrics.
Add a check that blocks release if accuracy drops.
Record a walkthrough of the pipeline and the gate.

exercises.title: Evaluate an LLM feature
steps: Pick a small task (for example classifying support tickets) and write 20 test cases.
Run them against your AI model and score the results.
Record yourself explaining what improved and how you know.

exercises.title: Monitor for drift
steps: Simulate a shift in your input data.
Show a metric that catches it.
Record a short explanation of what you'd alert on and what you'd do next.

practice.title: AI MLOps Engineer
practice.summary: Practice interview for an AI MLOps engineer: delivery pipelines for models, serving, evaluation and monitoring.

competencies.name: Model delivery
competencies.description: Takes models to production reproducibly and safely.

anchors.5: Built end-to-end pipelines with evaluation gates, rollout and rollback.

anchors.3: Set up or improved serving with one concrete decision.
anchors.5: Served several models under real constraints with measured results.

anchors.3: Built a test set and measured changes.
anchors.5: Runs regression evaluations that block bad releases.

competencies.name: Monitoring
competencies.description: Notices and fixes quality, drift and cost problems.

anchors.3: Monitors quality or drift and acted on it.
anchors.5: Covers quality, drift, latency and cost and changed something as a result.

questions.text: Tell me about a time you took a model into production. What made it safe to release?
Tell me about a model or AI service you ran in production. What serving decisions did you make?
How would you test that a change to an LLM prompt didn't make answers worse?
Imagine a model's answers slowly get worse over a month. What would you put in place?
Tell me about a time you reduced the cost or latency of a model in production.

practice.company_facts: This is a practice interview. There is no real employer: questions about pay, hours or the team can't be answered here.

settings.next_steps: Your coaching feedback appears as soon as the interview ends.
